key_terms: A producer with a transactional identifier that initializes, begins, sends, then commits or aborts, so records across partitions become visible together or not at all.
A consumer isolation level that returns only records from committed transactions and skips aborted transactional data.
The isolation level under which a consumer also observes records from aborted transactions.
A marker the broker writes into a partition to record that a transaction committed or aborted.
Rejecting an older producer instance that shares a transactional identifier with a newer one, so a stale instance cannot complete a transaction.
evidence: Actual owned Docker workshop observations, with source, failure and lifecycle scope stated separately. Commands are not executed by the classroom pad.
